# openlab 0.1.0 Preview

The first public preview of **openlab**, the research workbench: an agent you can watch, a
real workspace, and every result you can reproduce.

## What is inside

- **A session, not a chat box.** Each session is an experiment with a folder, a branch and a
  phase.
- **Every step is on the record.** A turn shows what the model thought, what it ran and what
  changed.
- **Your model, your terms.** No vendor is baked in. Bring a key, point at a lab server, or run
  a local model.
- **Reproducible by construction.** Statistical results come back with the R and Python that
  recompute them.

## Download

| Platform | Build |
| --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple silicon) | `openlab_0.1.0_aarch64.dmg` |
| macOS (Intel) | `openlab_0.1.0_x64.dmg` |
| Windows (x64) | `openlab_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe` |
| Linux (Debian, Ubuntu) | `openlab_0.1.0_amd64.deb` |
| Linux (Fedora, RHEL) | `openlab-0.1.0-1.x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux (portable) | `openlab_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage` |

## macOS: allow the first launch

These preview builds are signed ad hoc, not notarized, so macOS blocks the first launch. This
is expected, and it happens once.

1. Open the DMG and drag **openlab** to **Applications**.
2. Open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and scroll to **Security**.
3. Next to the message about openlab, click **Open Anyway**.
4. Confirm with **Open**.

Alternatively, right-click **openlab** in Applications and choose **Open**.

A signed and notarized release will open without this step.

## Other platforms

- **Windows:** SmartScreen may warn about the installer. Choose **More info > Run anyway**.
- **Linux:** if the AppImage is not executable, run
  `chmod +x openlab_0.1.0_amd64.AppImage`, then start it as usual.

## About this build

- Free and MIT licensed.
- The optional PDF scan engine (embedding server) is not included in this preview. The rest of
  the workbench works.
- Report issues at https://github.com/sciencedeltacom/openlab/issues.

A signed and notarized 0.1.x release follows once the Apple and Windows signing identities are
configured.
